title: You don't need ONE prioritization framework
description:
Most PMs argue about which prioritization framework is "the right one" — RICE, MoSCoW, value vs. effort. The real move is using all three in sequence: triage fast, rank the survivors, then scope the winner. Here's the three-step pipeline from the lesson, with the worked example that shows it end to end.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/product-manager-mastery-path/level-1/04-prioritization-basics/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Everyone argues about which prioritization framework is the best one. RICE, MoSCoW, value versus effort. Here's the trick: you're not supposed to pick just one.
Say you've got twenty backlog items. First, sort them fast into a value-versus-effort grid. That alone lets you toss the low-value, high-effort pile without any deep analysis.

display.heading: Step 1: Value vs. Effort
display.subheading: Fast triage of a long backlog -- not the final call

beats.narration: The survivors that are left get RICE-scored: reach times impact times confidence, divided by effort. That's how a handful of finalists get ranked with real numbers, not gut feel.

display.heading: Step 2: RICE
display.subheading: (Reach x Impact x Confidence) / Effort -- for a defensible ranking

beats.narration: Once the winner's picked, MoSCoW scopes the release: what's a Must, a Should, a Could -- and what's explicitly a Won't. Writing down 'Won't' kills scope-creep arguments before they start.

display.heading: Step 3: MoSCoW
display.subheading: Must / Should / Could / Won't -- for THIS release

beats.narration: Triage, rank, then scope. Three frameworks, one pipeline. The full worked example is in the lesson.
